title: What's the best AI tool for making a Hollow Knight-style game?
author: Z3rtox2310
selftext:
I want to try making a game inspired by Hollow Knight, with around 30 minutes to 1 hour of gameplay. I don't have much experience with game development, so I'm looking for an AI tool that can help me build the game, including things like combat, movement, enemies, level design, and abilities.

What would be the best AI tool for this? I'd prefer something that can help me create an actual playable game, not just generate code or artwork.

I'd really appreciate any recommendations or personal experiences. Thanks!

comments.author: loulo88
comments.body: Honestly there isn't one tool that spits out a playable metroidvania yet. What works better is picking a real engine (Godot is great for 2D and free) and using an AI coding assistant alongside it to write and explain the scripts as you go. Start tiny: get the player movement and one attack feeling good in a single room before touching enemies or abilities, because in a Hollow Knight-like the movement feel is basically the whole game. Once that's solid, adding a dash or wall jump one at a time is very doable even as a beginner.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
I would start with Claude Code + Opus 5.5, or Codex + GPT Sol 6.1. These are both good starting points. Grab an engine (Godot or Unity) and set up an MCP or cli tools so the AI can control the engine somewhat.

You will primarily be using the AI to write code and help you set things up in the engine.

Things like level design are going to be mostly you—design your levels, place enemies, that sort of thing.

I would start with pre-made assets from places like itch.io. It takes a while to figure out how to make assets with AI, and you may find it frustrating to get that working. Better to just start with pre-made assets, that way you can actually make a game. My game is still all pre-made assets and I haven’t yet gotten AI-generated assets that are better.

Some people will tell you that you don’t need an engine. It’s true that you don’t need an engine, but you’ll make much faster process and probably end up with something better, if you start with an existing engine like Unity or Godot.

It’s still a lot of work. Focus on getting something small and playable, like just a character that jumps around on platforms first. Nobody is one-shotting anything good.

Ask the AI to explain to you how to get started. “I want to make a game with AI, inspired by Hollow Knight. I have Godot installed and want to use that. How do I get started?”

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: get a $20 anthropic subscription, download Claude Code and tell Opus 5.5 to make you "a playable Hollow Knight game <and whatever additional stuff you want in it>" and then wait around 20 minutes.
